narrative: Fire and climate themes led today's batch: remote sensing revealed post-fire forest composition shifts in boreal Eastern Siberia, and a multispecies seed-addition experiment showed climate-driven range shifts lag at species' leading but not trailing range edges. Movement and behaviour work traced how drought reshapes large-carnivore habitat selection and elephant space use across timescales, while a long-running Swedish time series linked apex-predator and prey dynamics to mesopredator behaviour. Trophic and symbiosis contributions advanced methods toolkits, including a superposition approach for reconstructing food webs, a new Bayesian dynamic mixing model for isotopic diet estimation, and evidence that fungal guilds diverge sharply in climate sensitivity depending on their ecological role. Invasion biology ranged from axis-specific niche reorganisation in invasive crayfish to selection on genome size in globally invasive ragweed. Grazing and herbivory studies linked livestock risk-reduction strategies to rangeland use patterns and traced how goose herbivory reshapes microbial functional potential in sub-Arctic wetlands. Conservation papers questioned whether current protected-area category frameworks still fit a 'polycrisis' world and found uneven outcomes for border protected areas, while new zero-shot bioacoustic classifiers extended frog-call and individual bird identification across continents.
